tooling: git and git-lfs for model files, web downloader, and platform API and CLI at ai.gitee.com/docs. Documentation endpoint moark.com/docs returns HTTP 404.
chaining: Inherits the Gitee account quota if the repo lives on Gitee proper. Which would cap it at 5 GB, making chaining the only route and a poor one.

limits_note: The parent Gitee free account is the constraint and it is documented precisely: 1,000 repos, 500 MB per repo, 50 MB per file, 5 GB total across all personal and organizational repos, plus 100 MB per attachment and 1 GB of attachments per repo.
reliability_note: Gitee has a history of public-repo review and takedowns of content it dislikes, which for a mutable repo is a technical availability risk. The AI platform itself is a rebrand in progress (Gitee AI -> 模力方舟 -> moark.com), so links churn.

dead_end.why: Not published. Gitee's help centre documents the AI-model hosting flow (models are stored as LFS files inside a Gitee-style repo and the UI annotates each with its size), and 模力方舟 is presented as the successor platform that '同步了全球最热门的开源大模型和数据集' (mirrors the world's most popular open models and datasets). But the underlying Gitee free account is tiny, and I found no separate storage grant for the AI platform.
dead_end.retry_when: if the free allowance rises above 500 GiB per unit

extras.agent_focus: New and up-and-coming competitors to Hugging Face and ModelScope, judged on the hard test the brief sets: a credible HF competitor must permit multi-TB objects and generous per-account storage, because model weights and datasets routinely run to hundreds of GB / TiB. Split into three classes — Chinese domestic hubs (HF is blocked there, so a separate ecosystem exists), Western MLOps artifact stores (W&B/Comet/ClearML/Lightning/Deep Lake), and dataset-publishing startups (Source Cooperative, Oxen, OpenDataLab). Excluded and not re-reported: Hugging Face, ModelScope, Kaggle, Civitai, Ollama, Replicate, DagsHub, OpenML, fal.ai, Baseten, Modal.

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
